Austin-based Kettlebell Kings has become a small powerhouse in the world of home gym equipment—and these powder-coated models are no exception. Made from single-cast iron with a smooth-yet-grippy powder coat finish, these kettlebells are built to withstand endless swings, snatches, and cleans. The 18 available weight options (ranging from 9 to 106 pounds) make it easy to scale up over time, and the color-coded bands around the handles let you identify weights at a glance.

That quality comes at a cost. Kettlebell Kings’ kettlebells sit at the higher end of the price range—expect to pay around $500 for a full set. But if you want top-tier, American-made bells that’ll last forever, start here. "Whether I’m repping through a set of swings or snatches, I know I can depend on the durable, powder-coated weights," says MH Senior Fitness Editor Brett Williams, NASM.

Metal kettlebells are pricey. And they’re not exactly gentle on your wrists or floors. GoRuck’s Sand Kettlebell is a soft-sided alternative built for tough workouts and easy transport. Shaped like a traditional kettlebell, this canvas training tool can be filled with sand (not included), emptied when not in use, and folded up for on-the-go sessions.

It’s rugged as hell. The double-seal filling system keeps sand from leaking mid-workout. The padded handles add comfort, and GoRuck uses double-pass stitching and a reinforced base to keep the bag from falling apart, even after years of swings, presses, throws, and drops.

Just know this isn’t a direct substitute for a cast-iron bell. If you’re training for kettlebell sport or focusing on technique-heavy movements like snatches or Turkish get-ups, this won’t replicate the same feel. But for general strength and conditioning, it’s a versatile, joint-friendly, and durable option at a fraction of the price.

Plyo box workouts are a great way to build explosive strength, but not at the expense of your shins. REP’s soft plyo boxes feature a wood core and a high-density foam exterior wrapped in grippy vinyl, offering a good balance of structure and comfort.

They come in three heights—16, 20, and 24 inches—and arrive fully assembled. The soft covering helps muffle noise and reduces injury risk if you miss a rep. And while they’re relatively lightweight, each box can handle up to 400 pounds, making them suitable for bigger athletes or weighted jump work.

One thing to note: These boxes aren’t ideal on slick surfaces like tile, polished wood, or smooth concrete. They need some grip to stay put during explosive movements (we’ve made this mistake before). Also, the narrow footprint may feel less stable during lateral movements or box step-overs.

Still, for most home gym users, the REP Plyo Boxes offer a safer, quieter, and more versatile upgrade over the typical wooden box.

Read More: The 7 Best Plyo Boxes According to Certified Trainers

The Hydrow Wave earned a spot on our 2025 Men's Health Home Gym Awards. It pairs a sleek, compact design with surprisingly tranquil, waterway-inspired workouts. Unlike traditional rowers that use noisy air resistance (looking at you, Concept2), the Hydrow Wave uses magnetic resistance for a whisper-quiet ride that won’t disturb the rest of the house.

Yes, it’s pricey. And yes, you’ll need a monthly subscription. But Hydrow’s instructor-led, on-the-water sessions are so vivid and immersive that even longer workouts fly by. Samuel said it feels like you’re actually on the water, and his workouts rarely felt boring on this rower. When your workout is over, just fold it up and store it vertically to save space.

Our only gripe? You can’t skip the scenic classes and program your own intervals. Still, for most users, the guided experience is the main appeal. And when you’re done, the Wave folds upright for easy storage.

The Concept2 RowErg is the standard by which all rowing machines are measured, a device that can redline your heart rate in minutes and is perfect for strengthening hips, glutes, back, and core.

The RowErg with Standard Legs is the new name for Concept2's RowErg rower, and it's the first device that comes to mind when we think of training on a rower at home. Our editors have never been on a better rower than this one, point blank. In a nutshell, it offers many of the same features as the best rowing machines that cost twice as much.

"It's an industry standard used by CrossFit and in many high-profile competitions for a reason," Samuel says. "It relies on a variable resistance flywheel that provides a constant challenge, making it great for high volume or experienced rowers."

It's also extremely easy to assemble (you can see a video of us assembling it here). In our experience (and many Amazon reviewers agree), setup takes around 20 minutes with minimal tools or hardware (just eight screws are required). City dwellers and space-conscious users will appreciate the clever design that lets this machine separate into two pieces for easy storage. Built-in caster wheels make setup and put-away a breeze. Plus, it's surprisingly affordable. This is the definitive home rowing experience.

You can spend $25, $70, even $150 on a jump rope. But you don’t have to. After testing dozens, Men’s Health editors agree: The $6 BOOMIBOO Skipping Rope offers the best bang for your buck. It’s lightweight, durable, and surprisingly smooth thanks to ball-bearing rotation in the handles.

I’ve used this rope regularly for over a year, and it’s held up better than expected. The bearings spin clean, and the foam handles are easy on the hands. My only issue with it is that the length feels a bit off out of the package. You can adjust it (it comes at 9 feet), but I never bothered. I just widened my arms, and it still did the job.

Unless you’re chasing double-unders or elite-level speed, this rope is more than enough—and the price is tough to beat.

Read More: Best Jumping Ropes, Tested By Us

This adjustable weighted jump rope is made of thick silicone that is soft, sweat-resistant, and comfortable for long workouts. Our testing confirms this jump rope is built to last. Out of the box, it's nearly 10 feet long, but is designed to be cut to achieve the perfect fit based on user height. This is ideal for a single user, but doesn't lend itself well to multiple users within the same household unless they're the same height.

Together, the rope and handles weigh 1 pound, so this kit is enough to challenge you during a good cardio sesh. At around $20, this is another great budget-friendly option for anyone looking to get in some cardio at home without a huge piece of equipment.

When you're looking for an exercise bike that's as high-tech as it gets, the Peloton Bike is still our go-to choice. The 22-inch HD touchscreen display is crisp and easy to use, and its library of best-in-class instructor-led studio-style classes is a true game-changer for home workouts. Our editors have used this bike for more than four years now, and have never run out of fresh classes to try.

For nearly $1500, it's a bummer that users need to shell out an additional $24/month for full access to the platform. But for the many Peloton users who have found community in their classes and on the leaderboard, the cost is more than worth it.

Read More: The Best Exercise Bikes, Tested by Us

Manual treadmills may look intimidating, but they have surged in popularity for good reason: They make you work harder, respond instantly to your pace, and run quieter than motorized options. The REP Fitness Strive Treadmill is a standout in the category; it’s a durable curved treadmill that honors its promise as a manuel treadmill and adds a sled push to the equation.

At over 418 pounds, we suggest building this treadmill where you want it and avoid moving it up and down stairs. Still, built-in front wheels let you reposition it if needed. The 400-pound weight capacity makes it a solid pick for larger users, and REP Fitness backs its promise with a 5-year frame warranty—essentially guaranteeing long-term durability.

Yes, it’s big. Yes, it costs almost $4,000. But for runners or serious home gym owners looking for a low-maintenance, high-performance machine, the Strive Treadmill is a wise investment.

NordicTrack is a giant in the treadmill game, and the T10 hits the sweet spot for home gym owners. It’s more compact than the brand’s Commercial 1750, yet still boasts a full-size 60-inch running belt—long enough for sprinting and tall runners alike. Plus, it folds up for easier storage between workouts.

Despite its smaller footprint, the T10 packs in features. You can run up to 12 mph (a 5:00-mile pace) and incline up to 12%. The 10-inch touchscreen pairs with iFit for trainer-led classes, and the Follow Trainer mode automatically adjusts your incline and speed in real time to match the instructor’s terrain.

SmartAdjust learns your fitness level and tailors your workouts based on how you train, while ActivePulse adjusts intensity based on your heart rate (if paired with a compatible monitor). It’s a smart, sturdy, and space-conscious treadmill that’s ideal for intermediate to advanced runners who want a guided experience at home.

Are you aiming to build muscle like a Greek god or shed those pesky love handles? Different goals call for different equipment. If you're into strength training, focus on getting some quality adjustable dumbbells or a full rack setup. For cardio enthusiasts, a treadmill, stationary bike, or rowing machine will get your heart pumping and your sweat dripping.

Unless you're living in a mansion, your home gym likely won't be as spacious as a commercial one. So choose equipment that fits your available space. If you're tight on space, consider compact options like resistance bands or adjustable dumbbells. They're small but mighty, perfect for those who need to optimize their space.

And quality matters, man! Don't skimp on the good stuff. You want equipment that can handle your beastly workouts without falling apart like a house of cards. Look for trusted brands that have a reputation for durability and longevity. Read reviews, ask around, and do your homework. You don't want wobbly machines or weights that crack under pressure. Go for sturdy materials and solid construction. You'll be glad in the long run.

It may be the spice of life, but contrary to what the market may tell you, the basics let you perform the largest variety of movements. Pass on over-specialized tools that let you do a few unique exercises and nothing more. Dumbbells and kettlebells let you do a mix of explosive and controlled isolation moves and can help you build strength, power, and mobility. Opt for those over stability balls and suspension trainers, which require fancier setups (especially if you're building a living room facility).

Set a budget and stick to it. Home gym equipment comes in a wide range of price points, and it's easy to get carried away. Determine how much you're willing to spend and prioritize your purchases accordingly. Remember, it's better to invest in a few quality pieces than to clutter your space with cheap, flimsy gear that won't stand the test of time.

As the Fitness and Commerce Editor at Men's Health, I test and evaluate the best home gym equipment. I collaborated with our team of fitness editors and certified trainers to identify the best home gym equipment worthy of a recommendation, both new and tried-and-true. We spent months hands-on vetting products from top fitness brands, including cardio machines, weights, connected fitness gear, and more.

In fact, we've tested hundreds of pieces of equipment over the years, from the highest-end, commercial-grade models to budget gear from Amazon. Our extensive testing process involved a comprehensive evaluation of multiple factors, including durability, performance, suitability for different fitness levels, and value, to ensure that we recommend only the best. To gather diverse perspectives, we consulted our MH Advisory Board and Strength in Diversity trainers, who shared valuable feedback on the top home gym equipment based on their expertise and experience.

Here are 35 can't-miss items we would include in our dream home gym, with picks that work for just about every space and training style.

So, you're thinking about setting up your very own home gym. Well, buckle up because it's going to be a game-changer.

Convenience is the name of the game. No more wasting precious time commuting to the gym or waiting for your turn on the bench. With a home gym, you're the boss of your own fitness kingdom. You can squeeze in a workout whenever it suits you, whether it's before the crack of dawn or after a long day at work, or in bite-sized bits between meetings. Plus, no more crowds or sweaty gym rats hogging the equipment. It's just you, your favorite tunes, and some iron to conquer.

Sure, creating a lasting home gym demands an initial investment, but it's a wise long-term savings strategy.

Consider adjustable dumbbells (priced between $400 and $800), a yoga mat (typically $20 to $140), and a cardio machine like a rower or bike (average cost around $2000). While that initial investment may seem steep, keep in mind that the average gym membership in the U.S. is about $55/month, plus initiation and cancellation fees. You'll recoup your investment in less than 5 years.

There's nothing worse than investing in a new piece of home gym equipment, only to find it's a one-trick pony you're bored with after a week. For an at-home setup that will keep you excited to use it, you want gear versatile enough to work in different ways. That way, you can keep your space uncluttered and your budget on-point.

When it comes to the best bang-for-your-buck, value-packed equipment, our answer might annoy you. But all you really need? A pair of reliable adjustable dumbbells, a training program, and a weight bench.

Start out strong with a pair of adjustable dumbbells like the ones from SMRTFT or PowerBlock. Yes, they're pricey, but they pack a ton of versatility in a minimal footprint. Pair it with a weight bench like the one from REP Fitness, or a luxe option like this one from Prime Fitness.

To make the most of your equipment, consider a training app like our very own All/Out Studio, which is packed with thousands of programs and guided workouts to keep you engaged and challenged with whatever gear you're working with.

Top it off with a non-slip yoga mat like Lululemon's The Reversible (Un) Mat for a sweat-proof surface for floor exercises, and you've got a recipe for success.

Charles Thorp is the Fitness and Reviews Editor at Men’s Health, where he shares the best product recommendations in gym equipment, recovery tools, supplements, and more. #4984. Tron, Tether and Chainalysis Form a New Crypto-Crime Task Force—Replacing One That Just Collapsed

Tron, Tether and Chainalysis Form a New Crypto-Crime Task Force—Replacing One That Just Collapsed

Tron, Tether, and blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis have launched a joint effort to hunt down and disrupt criminal activity involving the USDT stablecoin, just weeks after a nearly identical alliance, with a different analytics partner, quietly fell apart.

Announced Wednesday, the Digital Crime Task Force aims to identify illicit activity involving Tether’s USDT on the Tron blockchain and surface it for law enforcement before criminals can move their funds.

The pitch is a shift from reactive to proactive: rather than waiting for a victim to report a crime or an investigator to flag tainted funds, the group says it will proactively trace criminal networks and coordinate asset freezes, drawing on Chainalysis’s intelligence and AI-powered investigative tools. It will also accept tips and freeze requests from police.

“Criminals are using AI to move faster than ever, and waiting for a victim to report a crime is no longer good enough,” said Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino, noting the company has frozen more than $7 billion tied to illicit activity while working with over 360 law enforcement agencies across 73 countries.

Tron founder Justin Sun framed it as protecting the millions who rely on USDT, which circulates on Tron to the tune of more than $94 billion.

The notable wrinkle is what this new alliance replaces. Tron and Tether previously ran a similar operation, the T3 Financial Crime Unit, formed in 2024 with rival analytics firm TRM Labs and later joined by Binance. Together, the group froze more than $450 million in tainted assets.

But Bloomberg reported earlier this month that T3 was quietly disbanded in late August, with people familiar citing slow response times and a lack of coordination among its members. Its collapse went public just days before the record $6.4 billion Binance hack.

Swapping TRM for Chainalysis is a pointed move, given the two are fierce competitors. Chainalysis has even sued the U.S. government over an ICE contract awarded to TRM without competitive bidding, underscoring the rivalry now running through crypto’s crime-fighting infrastructure.

The new task force says it will target a broad sweep of threats, from romance and investment scams to stolen funds, terrorist financing, North Korean cyber operations, cartel money laundering and child-exploitation material.

The group also framed the effort around a coming era of autonomous AI agents transacting onchain, which it warned will open fresh avenues for criminal exploitation.

#4979. Binance CSO unwittingly foreshadowed $6.3B hack tactic months before attack

In a July interview, Binance chief security officer Jimmy Su explained how fake coding assessments could compromise employee devices, a tactic later used in the exchange’s record-breaking hack.

Months before Binance lost $6.3 billion to a hack, its chief security officer described to Cointelegraph how a fake job interview could give attackers a foothold inside the exchange — closely resembling one of the entry methods later used against the exchange.

During a July interview about Binance’s response to rising security threats, Jimmy Su told Cointelegraph that fake job interviews were “something we worry about a lot internally,” explaining how attackers could tailor a job opportunity to an employee before persuading them to run code as part of a technical assessment.

“And once that gets executed, the device is compromised and then they can start harvesting credentials,” Su said, adding that attackers could then use that to penetrate further into the network.

Su’s detailed warning about malicious coding assessments was not included in Cointelegraph’s July coverage, but takes on new significance following the biggest crypto exchange hack in history.

In September, a Binance software engineer downloaded a malicious coding assignment onto his work computer during a fake job interview. That compromise became part of the multistage attack that culminated in October’s theft, according to Binance’s preliminary investigation.

During the interview with Cointelegraph, Su had also anticipated why security tools might miss such a trap. A technical assessment could involve seemingly legitimate steps, such as downloading a code repository from GitHub, he explained in July.

“Each step is actually legitimate on its own. So a lot of the anti-virus tools may not be able to detect it and flag it,” he said.

Binance’s investigation subsequently described a similar detection failure, saying the assignment’s setup process executed malware that evaded its endpoint security tools through obfuscation and other evasion techniques.

Su told Cointelegraph that it was Binance’s responsibility to contain the risk when employees pursued outside opportunities on work computers.

“Of course employees can explore outside opportunities. What we do worry about is that they do so on the company device,” he said. If an employee fell for a fake interview, he added, “the onus is on us to detect it,” and to “stop the actual execution of that code.”

Related: North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic

Binance was already testing employees against fake recruiters. Su said its internal red team had been conducting monthly phishing simulations for three to four years, with remedial training for employees who failed.

“In the beginning, the security hygiene left a lot to be desired. But after this amount of time, the company has improved significantly,” he said.

Kevin Gibson of recruitment firm Proof of Search told Cointelegraph that the threat is also changing how some crypto employers assess prospective hires, with clients increasingly wanting to know whether candidates have been met in person.

“A number of our clients are now asking us straight up whether we’ve met a candidate in person,” Gibson said, adding that candidates personally met by a third-party recruiter have an advantage.

Employees, like in Binance’s case, can also become targets.

“In crypto, a dodgy job offer or a ‘quick catch-up call’ can be the first step in a multimillion-dollar hit,” he said.

Binance said it blocked 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyber threats so far this year, which is roughly one attack every five days.

Following October’s attack, Binance said it had tightened device controls, rebuilt affected wallet systems and internal AI tooling, strengthened access controls and revoked compromised credentials.

It also said it was increasing investment in endpoint protection and developer-environment security, and engaging independent cybersecurity experts to review the incident. Some technical details and security measures would remain confidential, it said.

#4977. The 10 Best Face Washes for Men in 2026, Tested by Grooming Editors

Soaps from Kiehl’s and Tower 28 came out on top in our testing.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

EVERY GOOD SKINCARE routine starts with the same thing—a quality face wash. Before you layer on serums, moisturizers, and eye creams, you need to clear the canvas. A face wash does exactly that by clearing away dirt and grime that accumulate on your skin while also helping prevent clogged pores that can trigger breakouts. That’s why it’s crucial to find the best face wash for you, no matter your skin type.

Wash your face every morning, night, and after heavy workouts to remove bacteria and sebum before they build up, says dermatologistDr. Anthony Rossi, MD. The best face washes for men go beyond cleaning: they hydrate, fight acne, and control excess oil. This first step in your routine is especially important if you live an active lifestyle. While cardio workouts boost circulation and support collagen production, sweat can leave your skin vulnerable to breakouts and irritation.

With so many products out there, finding the right one for your skin type and preferences can feel impossible. That’s why I spent the last two years testing every cleanser I could get my hands on to find the ten best face washes for virtually any skin type and price point.

A face wash is the cornerstone of any skincare routine—without it, the rest of your products won’t work as well. Choose one that’s gentle yet effective because even if your entire routine is just washing your face, you don’t want a cleanser that strips away your skin’s natural oils.

Matching your face wash to your skin type ensures it works with your skin’s natural needs, clears and balances your complexion, and primes your face for the products that follow.

We’ve been testing face washes and cleansers since this story was first published in 2021. As Men's Health's Grooming Editor, I’m also constantly trying out the latest releases to determine which are worth adding to your rotation. For this update, I considered picks from previous iterations of this roundup, as well as current favorites from fellow Men's Health writers and editors. This ultimately led to me testing over 50 face washes, evaluating their ingredients, feel, consistency, and effectiveness. Below is the culmination of this extensive hands-on research: the ten best face washes for men with any skin type or budget.

For active guys who want a no-nonsense soap that still feels luxurious, this cleanser from Kiehl's delivers. Formulated with hydrating glycerin and squalane—and free of parabens and fragrances—it thoroughly cleanses without stripping moisture. Its powerful ingredients clean and hydrate at the same time, leaving your skin soft, balanced, and primed for the rest of your routine.

Testing Notes: I’ve used Kiehl's cleanser for years and love its ultra-smooth formula that glides easily over my skin. I appreciate that it’s fragrance-free, making it ideal for sensitive skin. Lightweight, gentle, moisturizing, and nourishing, it’s one of the most versatile cleansers I’ve tried—perfect for any skin type. At $16 for 2.5 oz, it isn’t the cheapest option, but it’s still on the affordable side of the market. Because it foams so well, I only need a small amount for a full wash, and one container lasts me about two months with daily use. Overall, Kiehl's Ultra Facial Cleanser remains my go-to everyday face wash, no matter your skin type or budget.

This gel cleanser uses zinc, copper, and magnesium to support the skin’s natural defenses while boosting hydration. Aloe vera then locks in moisture and forms a soothing barrier, while oat calms irritation and comforts sensitive skin. Fragrance-free, it gently removes makeup, sunscreen, and daily buildup without stripping or irritating—even for the most reactive skin.

Testing Notes: I don’t have rosacea, but my skin is prone to redness, so I was excited to see this cleanser approved by the National Rosacea Society—and it didn’t disappoint. Whenever my skin flares up, I use it daily, and within a week or two (depending on severity), the redness quickly calms. Its silky consistency also leaves my skin feeling smooth, balanced, and healthy.

You can’t go wrong with a classic. This Cetaphil cleanser, formulated for combination to oily, sensitive skin, actively removes dirt and excess oil while protecting your skin’s natural barrier. The blend of B vitamins and glycerin nourishes as it cleanses, leaving your face refreshed, balanced, and never tight or dry.

Testing Notes: Cetaphil’s Daily Facial Cleanser delivers incredible value for its price. I love that it packs the same hero ingredients you’d see in pricier formulas, like glycerin and niacinamide, yet it’s gentle enough for even ultra-sensitive skin. It leaves my face feeling clean but never stripped, which makes it easy to reach for every day. My only gripe? I wish the pump dispenser worked more smoothly—it can be frustrating when I’m half-asleep and just want a quick wash.

Long before CeraVe went viral on TikTok, grooming experts swore by the drugstore brand for its high-quality ingredients at budget-friendly prices. A perfect example is this cleanser, packed with hydrating staples like hyaluronic acid and ceramides that strengthen the skin barrier while keeping moisture locked in.

Testing Notes: CeraVe’s Facial Cleanser is one of my go-to budget face washes because it’s easy to find online or in stores, and it simply works. I’ve been using CeraVe since my early 20s, and I can honestly say the formula has never let me down—it removes excess oil and grime without ever causing breakouts.

Shaped like a deodorant stick but designed for your face, this solid soap from Oars and Alps packs charcoal, a buzzy exfoliant that gently scrubs without irritation. I love that even a 1.4-oz container lasts over a month when used daily.

Testing Notes: Oars and Alps’ cleansing stick has become my go-to TSA-friendly face soap for traveling and camping. I love how portable it is and how easily it applies—just like my favorite deodorant—while still exfoliating and removing dirt. It easily fits in my Dopp kit, and I don’t need to worry about it leaking or opening. Plus, my face feels incredibly clean after each use, and a little product really does go a long way.

Finding a TSA-friendly cleanser that doesn't spill is hard. That's where Jaxon Lane's Shake and Wake comes in. It's a powder-to-cream product that gently exfoliates skin and cleans just as well as a liquid cleanser, thanks to a powerful combo of niacinamide, vitamin E, and vitamin C. In other words, it's a Dopp kit must-have.

Testing Notes: The first thing I noticed about this wash was its powdery consistency. What surprised me was how much I liked it—and how often I keep reaching for it, especially when traveling. Similar to Oars and Alps Solid Wash, there is minimal risk of spilling—and even if it did (which I’ve yet to experience), the powder will be far less destructive than liquid.

It feels ultra-gentle on my skin and transforms into a soap-like lather as soon as it hits water. The container is TSA-friendly, tightly sealed, and unlikely to leak, and since it’s powder, even a spill would be minimal and far less messy than a gel.

If you're somebody who loves the smell of the great outdoors, or that irreplaceable feeling felt (and smelt) the early morning after a night of camping, then this face wash is for you. Loaded with skin-boosting natural ingredients like aloe vera, caffeine, and charcoal, Dr. Squatch's face wash exfoliates, refreshes, and cleanses with the best of them.

Testing Notes: With its unique charcoal-backed texture and feel, this wash is one of the most rejuvenating options out there. But what really stands out is its understated, yet still attention-grabbing pine tar scent—subtle enough to avoid clashing with your cologne, but woodsy enough to raise the nostrils in the best way possible.

For those with sensitive or dry skin, there are few (if any) better skincare brands than La Roche-Posay. And the brand's cleanser is a perfect representation of why. Its niacinamide-backed formula is equally gentle and hydrating. Add in other moisturizing winners like glycerin, along with the lack of any skin-aggravating ingredients like heavy fragrances or sulfates, and you have one of the lowest risk, highest reward face washes on the market.

Testing Notes: I have sensitive skin and love this cleanser because it never irritates me. Even if your skin is less reactive, the creamy lather feels amazing during and after each wash. It’s gentle and leaves skin feeling hydrated and healthy.

Talk about value—at under $7 a container, it’s hard to find a more effective, affordable face wash for men than Harry’s. Best known for its stellar shave gear, the brand has quietly expanded into no-nonsense men’s skincare, including standouts like its facial moisturizer. This face wash follows the same formula: it packs low-key hydrators like eucalyptus and peppermint alongside gentle exfoliants like glycerin, delivering a no-BS cleanse that gets the job done without breaking the bank.

Testing Notes: Harry’s hasn’t strayed from its facial-hair roots, as this cleanser doubles as one of the best beard washes, softening whiskers and priming them for trimming or shaving. I also can’t overstate how foamy it gets; it not only strips away dirt and buildup but also makes each (already affordable) container last a long time.

Anyone who struggles with acne knows it takes over your routine, demanding protective, non-invasive, blemish-correcting products at every step. For that crucial first cleanse, Geologie’s new Acne Control Face Wash stands out as the best option. Even though it’s been on the market for barely a year, it has already become a staple for me whenever I’m facing a breakout, thanks to its 2 percent salicylic acid formula and silky-smooth application.

Testing Notes: I still reach for this wash whenever I feel a blemish or breakout coming on. The only drawback is that the gel feels a little stringy at first and needs plenty of water before it foams. Once it does, though, the lather expands quickly, and a dime-sized drop covers my entire face—making each bottle last for months.

Wash your face twice a day—morning and night. Just as important, pay attention to the products you use, avoiding harsh chemicals like sulfates and parabens. Choose a gentle cleanser for everyday use and keep an exfoliating scrub for two or three times a week. Apply the scrub with light pressure—fast, hard, and rough isn’t the answer. Overdoing it can damage your skin and create new problems. And always remember: everyone’s skin type is different. What works for one person might not work for another.

#4975. 'A Massive Mistake': Tech, AI and Crypto Founders React to Jensen Huang’s Nvidia Exit

'A Massive Mistake': Tech, AI and Crypto Founders React to Jensen Huang’s Nvidia Exit

Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang is out as CEO after 33 years, and some of the loudest names in crypto and artificial intelligence think the company just made a spectacular mistake.

On Thursday, Nvidia confirmed Huang’s resignation as president, CEO, and board member, and named longtime finance chief Colette Kress interim CEO. The move followed reports of two extramarital affairs, including one involving a businesswoman U.S. intelligence reportedly suspected of links to China, as well as concerns over a reported relationship with an Nvidia employee.

Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in a message to employees on Sunday. Nvidia said in a board statement that it had no reason to believe its secrets or national security were compromised, and its independent investigation remains underway. The allegations about foreign intelligence have not established that Huang knowingly provided information to a foreign government.

But even without any leaks, the scandal was enough for the board to decide to let him go.

The market did not welcome the transition. Nvidia shares fell 14% at Thursday’s opening bell; with more than $500 billion wiped from U.S. stocks in a single minute. The company that was once the most valuable in the world has now fallen to third on that list.

Nvidia was already under pressure before the scandal, and Huang’s departure raised a particular problem for a company built so closely around its founder: Who, exactly, can replace him?

Changpeng “CZ” Zhao, the Binance co-founder and one of crypto’s most influential executives, said “it's a mistake for Nvidia to let Jensen resign.” Bitcoin entrepreneur and former Kraken executive Dan Held agreed, writing, “He shouldn't have resigned,” and argued that Huang’s personal problems should be weighed against the company he built.

It's a mistake for Nvidia to let Jensen resign.

— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) November 12, 2026

U.S. intelligence officials reportedly assessed Alice Huang as a Chinese intelligence asset, but Nvidia says it has no reason to believe any secrets were compromised, and Singaporean authorities said they lacked sufficient evidence to establish that she committed a crime. As of today, no law enforcement agency has presented any hard evidence against Alice Huang.

Anthony Pompliano, the Bitcoin investor and commentator, moved the conversation from the boardroom to the technology itself. “Do not get distracted by the headlines,” he wrote. “Open-source AI is essential to the freedom of billions of people in the future.”

Open-source AI is essential to the freedom of billions of people in the future.

— Anthony Pompliano 🌪 (@APompliano) November 12, 2026

Surrounding it all is likely the most talked about conspiracy theory in the open-source AI sphere. The ousting was designed to hurt open-source developments, the speculation goes, since Nvidia is one of the leading voices in the open-source movement, which closed-source companies see as a threat.

For Voorhees, the controversy also prompted a practical question. “Is there a decentralized Hugging Face yet?” he asked, alluding to one of Huang’s stated commitments. In other words, the crypto solution to a potential platform bottleneck is to stop trusting a single platform.

That concern is more than a slogan for a founder whose Venice AI business is built around private access to open models. Voorhees previously told Decrypt that the antidote to excessive control over AI was “open-source decentralization.”

Some developers saw a deeper threat in Huang’s departure: the loss of a powerful corporate champion of downloadable AI models, whose underlying parameters, or weights, can be run outside the companies that built them.

The worry is that an Nvidia without Huang could become less willing to confront firms that keep their most advanced models behind proprietary services.

Jun Song, an open-source AI advocate and hardware entrepreneur, alleged that OpenAI and Anthropic had spent millions lobbying Congress to restrict open weights. He pointed to a “Pace the Frontier” campaign and argued that Huang responded by building the Open Secure AI Alliance, ending his post with, “And today, we lost him.”

OpenAI and Anthropic have spent millions lobbying the US Congress to ban open weights.

When they formed the "Pace the Frontier" group to push for strict limits on open models, Jensen stepped up right away.

He created the Open Secure Alliance to fight back.

Look at the list of… pic.twitter.com/OeasotcLO3

In July, Nvidia joined Microsoft, IBM, Hugging Face, and dozens of other organizations to launch the Open Secure AI Alliance, which works on open AI security tools and standards. Nvidia also backed a letter defending open weights against broad restrictions.

The broader conspiracy claim needs, of course, much more evidence. The Pacing the Frontier initiative is a statement from employees at several AI companies seeking tools to slow dangerous frontier development, not proof of a joint corporate campaign to ban all open-weight models or remove Huang.

OpenAI subsequently signed the pro-open-weight letter, while Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said explicitly that his company had never advocated such a ban.

Other posts on social media showed how much anxiety the debate had generated. A commenter replied to Song that they were now “counting on Huawei and Deepseek for the very survival of the OSS community.”

Huawei and Deepseek are two major Chinese companies, known for their open-source developments

I can't believe now I am counting on Huawei and Deepseek for the very survival of the OSS community. What a loss...

— Look4Newways (@sflk2026) November 12, 2026

The issue comes with a rather large business backdrop. Nvidia agreed in September to acquire the open-source AI repository Hugging Face for roughly $12.9 billion, subject to regulatory clearance, in a deal expected to close in the first half of 2027.

That arrangement could put both the hardware used to build AI and the largest hub used to distribute open models under one company’s influence—arguably, the most powerful company on earth.

Epic Games founder and CEO Tim Sweeney was among the highest-profile tech executives to condemn the exit. “A sad day for NVIDIA, developers, America, and all humanity,” he wrote, praising Huang for keeping innovation moving even as Nvidia grew into an enormous company.

A sad day for NVIDIA, developers, America, and all humanity. Jensen founded and ran one of the few companies to reach a massive scale while driving massive continued innovation and ubiquity, while others fell into the trap of ever-increasing extraction. https://t.co/AkS5XT9HF8

— Tim Sweeney (@TimSweeneyEpic) November 12, 2026

Perplexity AI co-founder and CEO Aravind Srinivas took a more personal approach. “Thank you Jensen Huang for 33 years of bold leadership,” he wrote. He also credited Huang’s generosity toward other founders, including himself, for helping shape the future of American AI.

Peter Steinberger, creator of the open-source OpenClaw agent and now at OpenAI, argued that the decision felt rushed. “If that spy’s goal was to destabilize one of the most successful American companies, they achieved their goal,” he wrote on X. “Ousting Jensen feels rushed and not right.”

If that Spy’s goal was to destabilize one of the most successful American companies, they achieved their goal. Ousting Jensen feels rushed and not right.

— Peter Steinberger (@steipete) November 12, 2026

Financial commentator The Kobeissi Letter had urged the board to consult shareholders before any decision, arguing that there was no obvious replacement and citing research on the costs of ousting successful CEOs. After the announcement, the account called the resignation “the most costly mistake of the AI Revolution.”

Former DWS executive and corporate-governance critic Desiree Fixler invoked directors’ fiduciary duty, saying the board should protect shareholders instead of indulging what she called a media frenzy.

In general, most of the reactions were supportive, separating personal affairs from business. The corporate espionage angle has apparently not swayed tech enthusiasts.

This Jensen Huang thing is so ugly. Guy takes a company from zero to absolute pinnacle, through blood, sweat, and tears, a pure founder’s founder, great products, makes so many people rich beyond their imaginations, champions open free local AI, and then the incumbent modern…

— Neil Woodfine (@nwoodfine) November 12, 2026

Not everyone outside that chorus thought the security questions could be set aside. North Dakota Republican Sen. Kevin Cramer had called for Huang’s exit, warning about the risk of blackmail and saying the internal investigation was insufficient. The concern from Washington has been largely uniform: the possibility of compromising pressure against the leader of a company central to U.S. AI infrastructure.

Meanwhile, President Donald Trump has remained supportive of Huang: “He’s definitely suffering,” he told the press. “I think he’ll be in good shape.”

Speculation about Huang’s next job spread just as quickly as criticism of his last one. Responding to an X user asking him to hire Huang, Elon Musk replied, “That would be an honor.”

Nvidia says its board is searching for a permanent CEO from inside and outside the company, with Kress running the business in the meantime. Its next scheduled earnings report is November 17, the first major financial update investors will receive after Huang’s departure.

#4968. South Korea to permit crypto withdrawal freezes during hacking threats

The move follows recent security incidents involving South Korean crypto exchanges, including GOPAX’s precautionary suspension of services and a $70,000 hot-wallet breach at Prabang.

South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) plans to allow crypto exchanges to suspend deposits and withdrawals when hacking is suspected, rather than waiting until a breach is confirmed, amid a push for stronger industry security.

On Thursday, the FSC said it would issue a no-action letter permitting preventive suspensions under certain conditions. Current rules prohibit exchanges from blocking withdrawals without legitimate grounds and explicitly allow restrictions only when a hacking incident is clearly established.

The regulator also called for round-the-clock monitoring and incident response, higher cold-wallet holdings, and stronger insurance coverage and reserves. The FSC said exchanges unable to monitor continuously would process deposits and withdrawals only during staffed hours and notify users in advance.

The move follows recent security incidents involving South Korean exchanges. On Friday, crypto exchange GOPAX suspended trading, deposits and standard withdrawals after receiving a hacking threat, although a representative said no breach had occurred. On Oct. 24, trading platform Prabang suspended services after detecting abnormal hot-wallet withdrawals, reporting about $70,000 in losses.

In October, the FSC identified cybersecurity deficiencies at 130 of 555 financial companies reviewed nationwide. It separately identified GOPAX operator Streami and Prabang among 16 companies involved in earlier security incidents.

#4967. Illinois Crypto Tax Draws Unlikely Alliance of DOJ, Banks and DeFi

Illinois Crypto Tax Draws Unlikely Alliance of DOJ, Banks and DeFi

An unusually broad coalition, spanning the U.S. Justice Department, Wall Street’s biggest lobby, the national Chamber of Commerce and a who’s-who of crypto firms, has thrown its weight behind a legal challenge to Illinois’ first-of-its-kind tax on digital asset transactions.

The groups filed briefs this month in Illinois state court supporting a lawsuit from the Crypto Council for Innovation and the Blockchain Association, which are asking a judge to strike down the state’s Digital Asset Tax Act and permanently block its enforcement.

The tax imposes a 0.2% levy on the full value of a digital asset every time an Illinois customer trades, transfers, or stores it through a broker, even when there’s no sale, gain, or change in ownership.

Critics have called it among the most punitive crypto taxes in the country, in part because Illinois imposes no comparable tax on dollars, gold, stocks or any other asset, and no other state has anything like it.

On Nov. 6, the Justice Department filed a statement of interest arguing the tax undermines federal policy and U.S. leadership in digital assets, calling it vague and discriminatory for singling out crypto for treatment no other asset faces.

The U.S. Chamber of Commerce and the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association, which represents hundreds of broker-dealers, banks and asset managers, filed an amicus brief warning the tax reaches well beyond crypto-native platforms to the traditional banks, custodians and advisers increasingly offering digital asset products.

A separate brief filed Nov. 11 brought together crypto’s heavy hitters, led by the DeFi Education Fund, Andreessen Horowitz, Paradigm and Uniswap, and including Aave Labs, Chainlink Labs, Solana Policy Institute, Phantom, Jito Labs, Multicoin Capital and Stand With Crypto.

Their filing argues the law’s definitions are so vague they could stretch to software developers and decentralized protocols that hold no customer funds and have no way to identify users or know where a transaction occurred. The brief noted an estimated 2.64 million Illinoisans hold digital assets, the fifth-highest total of any state.

“This tax is unclear, discriminatory, unconstitutional, and harmful to the future of finance,” CCI CEO Ji Hun Kim and Blockchain Association executive Ashok Pinto said in a joint statement.

The challenge dates to August. As Decrypt reported, Illinois agreed in October to pause the tax until July 1, 2027, buying time for the court fight now underway.

#4966. The 7 Best Portable Basketball Hoops and Systems for Any Yard or Driveway

If you want to ball out at home, these are the hoops for you.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

If you live by the "ball is life" moniker and you need to be able to play at home, a portable basketball hoop is a must. Portable basketball hoops don't require you to perform manual labor like digging a huge hole in the ground and pouring concrete, nor do they cost over a thousand bucks. Another plus to going portable? You can store your hoop come winter, thus lengthening its lifespan. It’s also a solid option for those who don't have the time, money, or space to install an in-ground option but still wanna toss their basketball shoes on and shoot around a bit quickly.

"I feel like the portable hoop is what transformed me into who I am," NBA shooting coach Chris Matthews (a.k.a. Lethal Shooter) says. "My cousin Justin and I would play on the portable hoop at his house when we couldn't make it to the playground. He had a garage light, and we would shoot all night."

You can make memories like that in whatever space you have for the court. But don't get caught buying a hoop that’s a waste of money. Not all hoops are the same, so we’re here to cut through the noise. Here are some of the best options we came up with.

Spalding makes a handful of portable goals, but the Momentous EZ is our favorite due to its value-driven price and ease of assembly. Spalding notes it takes about 30 minutes to put together. We found it took just over that time when following the instructions, which makes it the easiest goal to assemble in our book.

As Matthews notes, "The more portable a basketball hoop is, the better, so that everyone can move it. That's one reason I like the models from Spalding."

As for the materials in the hoop, the Momentous EZ comes with an acrylic backboard in either 50- or 54-inch sizing. You can also choose between a clear view back, an H-frame, or a steel H-frame (for added support and durability). We chose the steel H-frame to help prevent backboard damage. The theory behind the H-frame is that it should help absorb stress when someone dunks or hangs on the rim.

There's a hand crank for adjusting the height of the goal (simple to use if you have kids or if you want to do a driveway dunk contest). The base is wide and supportive and will hold up to 26 gallons of water or sand. If you're looking for a premium goal that won't set you back a thousand dollars, there's nothing better than this pick. Start here in your search. You won't regret it.

More: The 6 Best Basketballs for Indoor Games and Street Hoops

If you are looking for a portable goal that won't break the bank, this top-selling $250 model is worth a look. It's made to adjust to a wide range of height, from 4.8 feet to 10 feet. This means it appeals to everyone from small kids to adults. One cool idea you can do with this goal is you can lower it to its 4-foot setting and position it up against an in-ground pool—something other goals in this guide don't have a low enough range to make it suitable for pool hoops.

The biggest qualm about this one is the polycarbonate backboard. It won't last as long as acrylic, and you should expect a few good years out of it with a slight decline in bounce as it braves the changing of the seasons. One way to help preserve this goal, though, is to store it inside whenever possible to avoid weathering.

Lifetime is another brand that churns out long-lasting portable goals. This one is similar to the Spalding Momentous EZ with a wide acrylic backboard. The base is also just as sturdy as the Spalding EZ, and it has an ability to hold up to 35 gallons of water or sand. The downside of this goal to the Spalding EZ is it's not as fast of a setup, so you do need to lock in for at least two hours to get it up.

The upside? That would be the 4 extra inches of backboard, the reinforced rim, and the hand crank adjustment. The rim is thicker and outfitted with steel springs, which makes it a lot more capable for handling dunks. The hand crank makes adjusting the goal from 7.5 feet to 10 feet smoother and easier than the turning hand crank on the Spalding EZ goal.

The Spalding has the easier setup and price, but Lifetime has a few premium features that will make competitive play more fun.

The FORZA Adjustable Basketball Hoop and Post System earns its place as a “Best Adjustable Hoop for Growing Players” thanks to its flexible height settings and portable design. Built for both kids learning their first shots and adults looking for competitive backyard games, the hoop adjusts from youth-friendly heights to regulation size, making it a long-term investment rather than something your kids quickly outgrow. Its wheeled base also makes it easy to move across driveways or patios, adding convenience for families who want flexibility.

Designed for indoor or outdoor use, the hoop features a sturdy base and adjustable frame that can accommodate players of different ages and skill levels. This versatile hoop can come out when you're hosting weekend family games or serious practice sessions, but be stored when not in use. There are also optional upgrades available.

This model from IE Sports will help save you some cash while still providing decent play. Its made with a 44-inch polycarbonate backboard, which is great when it comes to saving money. The base and frame are similar in design to the Awii Sports option, so there's no worries on durability here.

Like mentioned prior, we don't really like the hand crank for adjusting the height; this goal has one. You've probably noticed the unique mini trampoline this goal comes with so you can pass the ball to yourself. We think it's an awesome feature, as it maximizes solo practice by allowing you to work on passing and catch-and-shoot drills. Overall, this goal is reliable, well-priced, and comes with a fun feature.

Remember how fun mini hoops are? This goal takes mini hoops to a whole other level with an adjustable height pole (up to 7 feet) and a sturdy base. Sure you could buy a cheap sub-$100 full size goal for your kids to play with, but for a similar price you get a much better build and a whole lot of fun.

Position it up to your pool for water mini hoops. Bring it down to your basement or put it in the garage for winter mini hoops. You get the point.

The Huupe Mini Hoop is the perfect nostalgia pick for any guy, regardless of age. It is quite literally the most portable hoop on our list, with the ability to be tossed on any door. This smart hoop has a wide variety of virtual games you can enjoy. The hoop comes with some heft, namely from the technology, which allows you to test your shot against others online, or even watch your favorite streaming apps.

"I think that mini hoops like the Huupe are another great option for families that don't have room in their garage or a driveway," Matthews says. "It's a great way to have kids to get energy out during the day, even when the weather is not ideal. They are easy to install, too."

In any case, it's easily installed using the classic over-the-door mount. You can also wall mount, but you need to buy those parts separately. There are special sensors throughout the device, which follow your shot as well as your distance from the hoop. This means it can reliably track your shot so you can get better after every game. One of our testers even said, "I enjoyed using this hoop to shoot around with my toddler daughter, and when I just wanted to play around a little bit by myself, it was awesome to get to watch the NBA playoffs on the screen as I shot."

Chris Matthews (aka Lethal Shooter) is a world-renowned shooting coach to NBA stars like Jaylen Brown, Dwight Howard, and Anthony Davis, and WNBA star Candice Parker.

Having spent countless hours as kids growing up playing pickup games in driveways, we know a thing or two about a solid portable basketball hoop. Men's Health Fitness and Commerce Editor Charles Thorp, NASM, has played lots of basketball and helped us dial in on the proper picks for this guide. Considering all those firsthand experiences led us to find the best of the best. Factors like backboard material, adjustability, and special design notes were considered in our selection process. We also took into account price, as some basketball goals provide a better overall value than others.

In addition, we also consulted world-renowned basketball shooting coach Chris Matthews (a.k.a. Lethal Shooter) on what makes for a good portable hoop. Our guide below represents our top picks, all approved by Matthews, of portable basketball hoops that will actually last for years to come. Keep scrolling to learn more.

Not every hoop is going to have the same adjustability in terms of how low or high you can raise it. This is crucial if you have little ones and want the whole family to partake in the fun. It’s also a great way to put on a dunk contest if you still have the bunnies, too. There are also different mechanisms built for adjusting, such as a hand crank, a telescoping pole, pneumatic assist, or a gas spring.

The types of materials used directly impact the long-term durability of your hoop. The two types of backboard materials to know about for portable basketball goals are acrylic and polycarbonate (there's also glass, but glass is used for professional backboards and is extremely rare on portable ones). Polycarbonate is going to be cheaper, but the tradeoff is that exposure to weather and UV light will make the backboard brittle and rigid over time. Acrylic is typically more expensive, but the benefit is that it's better suited for exposure to weather and UV light (acrylic is not affected by UV light like polycarbonate), plus you get a more responsive bounce.

Basketball rims are not all created equal. If you’ve ever been to a park court, you know what we mean—one slightly off shot and your ball rockets across the street. There are a few common materials you’ll see: steel and double-rimmed steel, powder-coated rims, and occasionally composite or plastic. You’ll also see that there are breakaway rims, standard, and flex.

To keep a portable basketball hoop in place, you'll need to fill its base with something. Most portable goals hold about 35 gallons, and you can either go with water or sand. We prefer sand because it dissipates well. Sand is also denser than water, so filling the base with sand is wiser for a more secure hold. However, choosing water makes it easier to empty the base and refill, making it easier to maneuver, especially if you need to move elsewhere in your driveway (or take it to your neighbor's for a friendly pickup game).

If you're curious about how much weight you need to keep your goal in place, a safe number is around 300 to 450 pounds. It sounds like a lot, but if you want to be safe and protect your goal, then more weight is always worth adding. And keep in mind that they all include wheels attached to the base to move them more easily. If you want to eliminate the labor of filling the base full, you can fill it to a point and then stack sandbags on top of the back of the goal to keep it in place. It won't be the most pleasing to look at, but it will allow you to move the goal around more easily.

Paying more gets you a better playing experience, especially when it comes to a wide acrylic backboard. A wider backboard makes it easier to shoot bank shots and perform layups, and the acrylic material will be much more responsive and last longer. A more expensive goal might also come with better wheels for moving the goal. Keep in mind a portable basketball hoop won't be as deluxe as an in-ground one, but you can get pretty dang close.

A regulation backboard is typically 48 inches tall by 72 inches wide. Most portable hoops have a 48-inch height, but there's a variance on width. While 72 inches is fun to play on due to the full ability to shoot bank shots and layups, a driveway goal doesn't need to be that wide.

Look to a 50-inch or 54-inch width. Anything under 50 is fine; however, you will lose space to shoot bank shots and layups. The benefit to buying a goal with a smaller backboard, though, is that you save money (they're almost always cheaper).

The easiest way to store a portable basketball goal is to lower the rim to its lowest setting, tarp it, then roll it into a garage or shed. Some basketball hoops can be disassembled (or at least partially disassembled), but that process can be pretty annoying. Make sure to drain any water from the base to avoid it freezing and expanding the plastic of the base.

Some of the high-end Spalding portable goals can partially disassemble for storage (not the Spalding EZ we recommend, though). You can take out bolts at the middle of the goal, and the backboard will fold down, thus helping store it in a garage or shed with a low ceiling.

#4963. BlackRock Bitcoin ETF outflows hit $2B over nine sessions

US spot Bitcoin ETF outflows rose to nearly $300 million on Wednesday, up from $95 million a day earlier, as five-session withdrawals reached $1.44 billion.

BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF), the iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), recorded more than $2 billion in net outflows over nine consecutive trading sessions through Wednesday.

Investors pulled a net $269.7 million from IBIT on Wednesday, accounting for about 90% of the day’s $300 million in net withdrawals across US spot Bitcoin ETFs, according to Farside Investors data.

Grayscale’s Bitcoin Trust ETF (GBTC) recorded $39.1 million in net withdrawals, while the Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust ETF (MSBT) drew $9 million in net inflows.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs posted nearly $1.44 billion in net withdrawals over five straight sessions. Wednesday’s increase followed three sessions of easing outflows.

Crypto exchange Bitfinex said on Wednesday that slowing ETF outflows could be an early step toward a market floor, but were not enough on their own to establish a recovery.

Bitfinex found that in the ETF outflow streaks it studied earlier this year, Bitcoin gained a median 6.4% over 10 trading sessions when the streaks ended with at least three consecutive sessions of net inflows.

Bitcoin traded near $73,000 at the time of writing, down 8.5% over the past week, according to CoinGecko.

In a Wednesday note shared with Cointelegraph, Laser Digital’s derivatives trading desk pointed to weak spot demand, a persistently negative Coinbase premium and large liquidations of leveraged long positions.

The desk said Bitcoin barely rose during Monday’s rebound in the Nasdaq, which gained almost 3%.

#4959. Ethlabs drops Hegotá slot proposal in push for 2027 quantum readiness

Ethlabs’ roadmap aims to help Ethereum withstand quantum attacks and give users a way to protect their accounts by 2027.

Ethereum research group Ethlabs said Wednesday it will withdraw its proposal to speed up the network’s block production from the planned Hegotá upgrade, urging core developers to prepare the network for quantum attacks by 2027.

On Wednesday, the group outlined “pqai27,” a proposed roadmap that aims to protect Ethereum against threats from quantum computing and increasingly capable artificial intelligence. It said unrelated upgrades should be reconsidered.

Ethlabs previously backed Ethereum Improvement Proposal (EIP)-8198, known as Quick Slots, which would initially cut Ethereum’s slot time from 12 seconds to 10 seconds. The group said it would redirect resources to pqai27 but will still pursue faster slots in 2028.

For Hegotá, Ethlabs said FOCIL, a planned censorship-resistance feature, should proceed only if it does not jeopardize quantum readiness. The group called Frame Transactions, which would enable more flexible account authentication, central to the proposed transition.

It said Glamsterdam, the upgrade before Hegotá, should proceed as planned.

Ethereum core developers have not approved the proposal. The Ethereum Foundation’s published roadmap still targets December 2029 for quantum resistance. At Devcon, researcher Justin Drake said he hopes to complete the transition in 2028.

Improve your game with the latest pickleball-ready shoes.

PICKLEBALL IS A fun way to stay fit, which is especially true if you have the proper gear. This ensures you can make the most of all your matches, which starts from the ground up. Buying a pair of pickleball shoes is one of the smartest investments you can make in your game. That means you want strong outsoles with responsive tread patterns and a midsole structure that can handle fast-twitch lateral movements. Pickleball shoes need to provide support, so buying the lightest shoe possible is not the smartest move. When buying a lightweight shoe (say, under 10 ounces) there's likely to be some sacrifice in support or stability. The trick? Stick to pickleball-specific shoes first. You can also consider tennis shoes and cross-trainers due to their similar support-first construction. Avoid featherlight running shoes that are built for a different type of movement.

Mesh is the most common and best material to look for in the upper of a pickleball shoe. However, like weight, you don't necessarily need the most breathable mesh possible. Some pickleball shoes sacrifice breathability to boost abrasion resistance, and to help keep your foot secure (like limiting your foot rolling and turning inside the shoe).

When it comes to the outsole, look for a shoe that has a strong rubber pattern that will help grip surfaces and reduce the odds of slipping when turning your feet. Some pickleball shoes pay greater attention to tread pattern, which can help provide a feeling of better grip on a court. Outsole will largely come down to personal preference, as most are constructed about the same.

When looking at the midsole, aim for a shoe that has supportive cushioning (like EVA foam) and keeps a relatively low profile. Prioritizing a midsole with too much cushioning could lead you to a shoe that sits high (like a Hoka running shoe), thus leading to a less responsive design, which could potentially lead to a greater chance of rolling an ankle when making fast turns on the court.

I have been fortunate enough to rock quite a few pairs of pickleball shoes over the past few years. Having played on multiple surfaces, I’ve learned a few things about what to look for when selecting a pair. I also partnered with our other writers and editors at Men's Health to help select the best pickleball shoes we’ve tested in the past few years, available. We’ve compiled a guide to the best all-day play, taking great note of each shoe's stability, durability, weight, and price point. Special consideration was taken into account for pickleball shoes that had excellent traction and stability since those two qualities are the most important in a pickleball shoe.

There is a lot of crossover from effective tennis shoes to pickleball shoes. With minimal differences, some of their picks made it to this guide.

If you're someone who's going to play pickleball once or twice for recreation, then you could get away with a low-profile running shoe. But if you're expecting to play any more than that, we strongly recommend buying a proper pair of pickleball shoes.

The reason we don't recommend wearing just any type of running shoe is that running shoes are made for forward motion, so there's often less emphasis on reinforcing the shoe for side-to-side movements. Running shoes also have less structure and stability than what you want in a pickleball shoe, as the running styles these days are made to be as lightweight and breathable as possible (with high cushioned stacks), which means less focus on overall support.

So, to be clear, you should steer from wearing running shoes for pickleball if you expect to play the game on a regular basis. A proper pickleball shoe is a smart investment that will help give you traction and stability while greatly decreasing the chance of rolling an ankle or spraining a knee.

#4955. Tron and Tether bring in Chainalysis after T3 crime unit folds

The group will focus on illicit USDT activity on Tron and help law enforcement investigate suspicious transfers and freeze funds faster.

Tron, Tether and Chainalysis announced a task force Thursday to identify and disrupt illicit activity involving USDT (USDT) stablecoin on the Tron blockchain.

The Digital Crime Task Force will use blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis’ data and AI tools to flag suspicious activity and give law enforcement leads to trace and freeze funds, according to an announcement shared with Cointelegraph.

Bloomberg reported on Nov. 4 that the T3 Financial Crime Unit, which Tron and Tether formed with TRM Labs in 2024, disbanded in late August. An unnamed source cited by the outlet said slow responses and poor coordination hampered the unit.

Cointelegraph contacted Tether, Tron and TRM Labs for comment but did not receive responses by publication time.

Related: Binance CSO unwittingly foreshadowed $6.3B hack tactic months before attack

The task force’s priorities include investment and romance scams, crypto theft, terrorist financing, North Korean cyber operations and cartel money laundering.

“Criminals are using AI to move faster than ever, and waiting for a victim to report a crime is no longer good enough,” Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said in the announcement. He put Tether’s cumulative USDT freezes at more than $7 billion.

USDT on Tron accounted for 99.9% of the $1.07 billion in crypto received by 34 casinos in Sihanoukville, a Cambodian city known as a hub for scam compounds, from Jan. 1 to Sept. 7, TRM Labs reported.

Casinos tied to US-sanctioned networks received $687 million of those inflows. TRM Labs cited low fees and deep liquidity as reasons for the widespread use of USDT on Tron in the region.

Following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, stolen funds were converted to USDT on Tron and cashed out through suspected Chinese over-the-counter trading services, according to blockchain intelligence company Elliptic.

During the record $6.3 billion Binance hack on Oct. 29, hackers swapped approximately $234 million in USDT for Tron’s native token (TRX) before Tether froze the remaining USDT in two wallets linked to the theft, according to Crystal Intelligence.

The US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed both hacks to North Korea. In a statement published by North Korean state media on Nov. 3, Kim Yo Jong rejected the Binance attribution and cited Bybit as another case in which she said Washington tried to blame Pyongyang.

#4954. Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom: The AI Stock Winners and Losers After Jensen Huang’s Ousting

Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom: The AI Stock Winners and Losers After Jensen Huang’s Ousting

Wall Street is picking winners and losers from Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, and the market is treating the chipmaker's competitors considerably better than companies tied to its business.

Nvidia shares fell 4.59% to $165.75 Thursday afternoon, recovering from an opening price of $151.01 and an intraday low of $148.80.

The rebound softened an initial collapse of more than 14%, but the stock remained firmly in negative territory.

The selloff followed Huang's immediate resignation as CEO, president, and board member after reports of extramarital affairs and allegations involving a suspected Chinese intelligence operative. Nvidia named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO, although the company has not established that corporate secrets were compromised.

The stock was already in trouble before Huang stepped down. Nvidia had lost approximately $1.27 trillion in market capitalization between October 6 and November 6, raising questions about AI spending even before the leadership crisis intensified.

AMD climbed 5.79% to $584.89 after opening at $569.28, making it one of the clearest beneficiaries of Thursday's trading.

The company competes directly with Nvidia in AI accelerators, and uncertainty around Nvidia's leadership could make customers more interested in diversifying their chip suppliers.

Broadcom followed a similar trajectory, gaining 5.65% to $364.73 from an opening price of $356.80.

Unlike AMD, which competes through its own GPU products, Broadcom specializes in custom AI processors and networking technology, offering large customers a different way to reduce their dependence on Nvidia.

Google’s parent company Alphabet also advanced, rising 2.06% to $299.49 after opening at $293.77.

Those alternatives existed before Huang resigned, and Thursday's gains do not establish that Nvidia has lost customers. Investors may simply be pricing in better competitive opportunities if the leadership transition disrupts Nvidia's strategy or customer relationships.

Nvidia-backed CoreWeave suffered a much rougher session, falling 7.49% to $56.22 after opening at $50.91.

Its decline came just one day after the cloud provider surged 24.7% following quarterly revenue growth of 168%, so this may be just as much a correction after an explosive movement as it is a reaction to Huang’s ousting.

In any case, the relationship between the companies helps explain the anxiety among investors. Nvidia invested another $2 billion in CoreWeave in January and has an initial $6.3 billion agreement to purchase unused computing capacity through April 2032, making it an investor, supplier, and customer of the same company.

Any change in Nvidia's investment priorities could therefore affect CoreWeave beyond ordinary chip purchases, although neither company has announced changes to those agreements.

The pressure also reached the semiconductor supply chain. TSMC, which manufactures Nvidia's advanced processors, fell 1.15% to $408.61 after opening at $394.62, while memory supplier Micron lost 2.70%, trading at $789.43 after opening at $769.31.

SK Hynix, another major supplier of high-bandwidth memory used in AI hardware, declined 3% to $137.98 from an opening price of $134.25.

These companies depend on broader chip demand, however, so their losses cannot be attributed entirely to Nvidia's leadership problems.

For investors, the immediate concern is less about whether AI chips will stop selling and more about how Nvidia manages its partnerships, financing commitments, and product roadmap without the executive who built much of that network.

Nvidia's board has said it expects operations and customer commitments to continue without interruption. The company is scheduled to report quarterly earnings on November 17, with Kress now leading the business through its first earnings announcement since Huang's departure.

#4952. Stablecoin supply falls $14.2B in biggest 30-day drop since June 2022

Crypto markets were left with “less fuel” to rally after the market cap of major stablecoins saw its biggest 30-day drop in over four years.

Stablecoin supply fell by $14.2 billion over 30 days, the biggest drop since June 2022, according to Glassnode.

The rolling 30-day contraction in stablecoin supply hit $14.2 billion this week, more than the $9.5 billion drop seen as Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $58,000 on July 1. It also marks the most pronounced drawdown since June 2022, when supply fell by nearly $30 billion.

Selected stablecoin supply data. Source: Glassnode

Stablecoin liquidity is a key yardstick for gauging crypto market sentiment.

“A shrinking supply means holders are redeeming stablecoins for dollars and taking that cash out of the market, which leaves less fuel for a rally,” Glassnode commented.

USDT, the largest stablecoin by market cap, continues to trade slightly below its $1 peg, per data from TradingView. Glassnode attributes the phenomenon to the “same pressure” from investors rotating out of the stablecoin market.

“Should the 30-day change turn back to growth, it would be the first sign that new money is coming in,” it added.

USDT/USD one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

Crypto market metrics continue to point to weakening demand as Bitcoin trades near 11-week lows.

Related: Bitcoin short-term holders send 47K BTC to exchanges at a loss

On Tuesday, onchain analytics platform CryptoQuant that its measure of Bitcoin demand fell by 284,000 BTC over 30 days, the most pronounced downturn since March 2025.

The Coinbase Premium Index, which measures the difference between Coinbase’s BTC/USD price and Binance’s BTC/USDT price, was still negative on Wednesday. The index fell to -0.27% on Oct. 29, its lowest level since November 2022.

“This unusually deep discount suggests weaker relative demand or greater selling pressure on Coinbase, a major venue for US-based trading activity,” CryptoQuant contributing analyst Amr Taha wrote at the time.

Bitcoin Coinbase Premium Index. Source: CryptoQuant

AS MEN, THE decision to go bald isn’t always one that’s made for us (thanks, genetics). But how you deal with hair loss is entirely in your hands. Sure, there are some viable hair loss treatments and shampoos for thinning hair that we certainly back. For many men, it's easier to just bite the bullet and shave their hair completely to offset any future thinning woes. If you are one of these men, more power to you! Hell, some men do it even if they’re not experiencing hair loss—and that’s cool, too. Investing in a quality head shaver will double down on the convenience factor of being bald by making the entire process seamless.

When you do choose to shave your head, the tools you use to do it are paramount. That’s where the best head shavers come in. These high-tech gadgets are specifically designed to make shaving your head easier, whether it’s through a multi-head ergonomic design or close-cutting technology (or both).

Far easier than heading to the barbershop every few days, these electric shavers are meant to be used at home. Think of them as an easier, safer, and quicker alternative to carefully taking a razor to your dome. But before investing in a shaver, there are a few key factors to keep in mind to ensure you select the absolute best one for you.

This tiny but powerful shaver is designed to give your scalp the closest shave possible, whether you prefer to do it dry, wet, or with the aid of other products. The five ScalpSafe shaving heads wrap around the curves of your head for a microscopically close shave, and the additional attachments, like a pre-shave exfoliation brush and precision trimmer, are nice bonuses.

Our editors also love that it pairs nicely with our favorite shaving creams and pre-shave oils, in case you want an even deeper cut. Its portable design makes it easy to carry in your luggage, though its travel case is sold separately. Not to mention, the five heads of this shaver definitely give an incredibly close shave—as close as the Remington and the Braun, both of which we found to be top of the heap in our testing process.

We also appreciate the additional attachments that this one comes with, unlike the Remington, particularly the pre-shave exfoliating brush, which not only helps give a closer shave, but also feels pretty damn good on your dome (you’ll want to only use this if you have a tiny bit of stubble though—the bristles aren’t long enough to reach through longer hair).

In theory, the trimmer attachment and the accompanying guards are great if you want to trim your beard (the brand also says you can use it to trim your body and other areas), but we found that the design of the device makes that difficult. Since it’s meant to be held in the palm of your hand, it’s not as easy to use on your face as a more traditional razor design like the Braun or even the Andis. We would probably skip that and relegate this device to only our heads, which, at a comparable price point to other models like the Remington, is OK.

If you’re in a rush, this easy-to-use shaver may be your answer. Thanks to the pivoting shaver heads that hug each curve of your head, the brand says that this device can shave your entire head in just two minutes.

After testing the Remington Balder Pro for over a year, we can safely say that it easily gave us a head shave in less than five minutes, which is great for guys who cut their dome weekly. We love the hair capture chamber, which collects hair for easy cleanup, and its non-slip grip gives you extra control when you're mowing through your head.

Keep in mind that this is designed only for head shaving, so if you’re looking for a more multi-purpose solution, you’ll want to go with a more traditional electric shaver like the Braun Series 9 Pro Plus. And since there aren’t any additional attachments like the kind that come with others, like the Freebird, you’re really only going to use this to give your head a smooth, clean shave (which it is frankly very good at doing).
